title: Kidney capsule transplantation of chemically treated embryonic murine tooth germs
protocol: Sacrifice the pregnant mouse at embryonic day (E) 13.5.
Dissect out the uterus; place it in a plastic Petri dish with cold phosphate buffered saline (PBS).
Cut the uterus between the implantation sites with scissors.
Transfer one embryo into a Petri dish with cold PBS and remove the uterus and decidua by using forceps.
Separate the head from the body using needles.
Transfer the isolated head to a glass Petri dish with cold PBS.
Separate the upper and lower jaws.
Remove the tongue from the lower jaw to visualize tooth germs.
Dissect developing tooth germs and place them in a glass Petri dish with cold PBS.
Culture dissected embryonic teeth in vitro for studying the effect of chemical disruption on tooth development.
Place dissected tooth germs on top of semisolid medium containing either 5 μM GI254023X or DMSO (vehicle).
Incubate at least 6 tooth germs in each Petri dish for early developmental stages.
Transfer embryonic teeth from cold PBS to the surface of semisolid medium in a plastic Petri dish.
Take one tooth at a time using a pipette (yellow tip) and place them on top of the semisolid medium.
Remove remaining liquid around each tooth once all are placed in the Petri dish.
Incubate teeth at 37°C until they reach the desired developmental stage (7 days).
Transfer developing teeth to fresh semisolid medium every 2–3 days.
Inject buprenorphine (0.1 mg/kg bodyweight) subcutaneously to recipient mouse 1 hour before surgery.
Anesthetize mice with inhalation anesthesia (isoflurane).
Apply vitamin A ointment to the eyes to prevent drying.
Put the mouse on one side, and make an incision exposing one kidney.
Make a small incision in the kidney capsule using forceps.
Lift the capsule and place the embryonic tooth under it securely.
Suture the animal with absorbable polyglycolic acid suture.
Close the skin incision with a metal clip.
Place the mouse on a warming pad.
Observe the mouse until it regains consciousness.
Mix 4%–5% isoflurane for induction.
Mix 1%–3% isoflurane for maintenance.
Stabilize the kidney using parafilm.
Make a linear cut in the middle of a rectangular-shaped piece of parafilm.
Place the parafilm to trap the kidney and prevent it from moving back into the abdominal cavity during transplantation.
Add sterile PBS to avoid drying of the surface of the kidney.
